story: Teaser, two stories: (a) the U.S. reportedly lets Britain test AI models early again (UK AI Security Institute); (b) Chinese mathematicians teamed up to build AI for maths. This file covers (a) as a generic scene only; (b) has no clip.

author: NASA Ames Research Center

has_text_logos: no clear text or logo in the cut at contact-sheet scale; a green digit '2' room sign is visible
notes: Cut = 10 s from t=71 s of the 244 s NASA B-roll 'Ames Research Center Unveils New Modular Supercomputing Facility' (Aitken supercomputer). Slow pan across rows of cabled server racks in a supercomputer room: a generic 'AI models on big computers, testing' scene, not the UK AI Security Institute or any UK government site. Original large file (168,368,761 bytes, md5 43c7d08de4b9807b69b49079f5707175) kept in the folder. NASA page exceptions: third-party content, commercial use of identifiable people, and NASA logos may need clearance; none is prominent in this cut. Contact sheets: contact_full.jpg (whole file, one frame per 6 s) and cut_contact.jpg. Story (b), maths AI: NO clip found. Candidates seen on Wikimedia Commons (Walter Lewin chalk.ogv, Solving-quadratic-equations.ogv, Nonlinear Systems lecture) were never licence-checked because every Wikimedia call returned HTTP 429 from 12:33 to 12:55 UTC (shared IP rate limit). archive.org maths items carry uploader-set licence flags only (not usable: not sure).
